matches.rationale: Finding pred_id 1 reports different inflated numbers (6.8× TTFT, 5.1–7.2× throughput) and identifies an abstract vs. intro/conclusion inconsistency, whereas GT1 describes abstract numbers (4.2×, 3.2–4.5×) being overstated relative to experimental figures—a different inconsistency with different values.
No finding addresses the burst tolerance definition contradiction in Equation 1 or any logical inconsistency in Section 3.1 load balancing.
No finding mentions missing baseline configuration details (batch sizes, KV cache, chunked prefill) for vLLM or DistServe.

Finding pred_id 2 identifies an arithmetic inconsistency in Figure 6 for DistServe's multiplier (4.5× label vs. ~250→450 actual), whereas GT4 concerns overstated ElasticMM throughput gains vs. vLLM in the text—different comparisons and different specific issues.
No finding reports the unsupported generalization about universal applicability across all MLLM architectures or the claim distortion in Section 4.2.
No finding mentions the fabricated reference [61] or any citation fabrication in the Related Work section.
No finding addresses Equation 3, the undefined β factor, or any logical inconsistency in the decode/prefill cost structure.
No finding mentions missing ethical disclosures, user consent, IRB review, or data provenance concerns for the datasets.
No finding captures the promotional claim that ElasticMM 'completely eliminates all inference bottlenecks' in the Introduction.
No finding addresses the mischaracterization of unified multimodal prefix caching as a scheduling mechanism in the abstract versus a separate optimization in Section 3.3.
No finding describes the ablation study misrepresentation where both optimizations are claimed to provide roughly equal gains.
No finding reports the unfair comparison involving ElasticMM's access to optimized CUDA kernels and custom memory allocators unavailable to baselines.
No finding discusses the Conclusion's absolute guarantee of SLO compliance under all workloads, which overstates the experimental evidence.
No finding mentions the false attribution of encoder-decoder MLLM architecture to Vaswani et al. in the Preliminaries section.
No finding reports the omission of limitations, failure modes, or societal impact discussion in the Conclusion.
